topIssues.title: [Epic] Ship the agentic parent suite with trustworthy household coordination
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Goal

Ship a trustworthy LifeOps parent-assistant suite that materially reduces the
anticipation, planning, coordination, monitoring, and recovery work carried by
a busy world-traveling mother coordinating children with a co-parent and
caregivers.

The completed system must ingest authoritative household sources, reason over
multiple calendars without leaking private event details, distinguish proposals
from agreements, obtain the right approvals, monitor material changes, execute
typed transactions exactly once, and verify closure. It must expose source
freshness and errors instead of presenting unavailable data as a healthy empty
state.

## Design doc

`packages/docs/ongoing-development/research/11-agentic-parent-suite.md`

## Scope

- Calendar source registry, sync health, multi-account aggregation, guest
  free/busy, ICS/webcal, and Microsoft Graph calendar support.
- Deterministic conflict/availability evaluation for time, people, custody,
  caregivers, transport, locations, resources, travel, recurrence, time zones,
  DST, and all-day events.
- Typed schedule proposals, per-party agreements, material-change
  invalidation, approval-gated messaging, and provider materialization.
- Household roles, scoped/expiring caregiver access, private-busy projection,
  append-only audit, and scoped export.
- School/activity ingestion and correction monitoring; action bundles,
  responsibility ownership, seasonal opportunities, household items, and
  external-source adapters.
- Food constraints, inventory confidence, cart/order idempotency, delivery
  exception recovery, childcare/work modeling, and source-grounded parenting
  guidance with human handoff.
- A composite world-traveling co-parent persona plus G1-G48 capability
  scenarios, real-provider tests, live-model trajectories, and manually
  reviewed evidence.

## Non-goals

- A second scheduler, household graph, connector abstraction, or file store.
- Behavior keyed from prompt text or demographic runtime modes.
- Autonomous sensitive messages, custody changes, medical/legal decisions, or
  purchases without typed policy and required approval.
- Scraping private guest calendars or fabricating availability, inventory,
  costs, source health, transactions, or completion.

## Work Items

- [ ] Ratify calendar-source health, proposal/agreement, access, audit,
      responsibility, provenance, and transaction contracts.
- [ ] Consolidate conflict detection and wire production guest free/busy.
- [ ] Route scheduling lifecycle communication through draft and approval
      policy.
- [ ] Implement provider-neutral sync, pagination, cursors, webhooks, and
      idempotent reconciliation.
- [ ] Implement Microsoft and hardened ICS/webcal sources.
- [ ] Implement household roles, scoped access, private-busy, audit, and export.
- [ ] Implement schedule proposals, approvals, materiality, and final
      calendar materialization.
- [ ] Implement school/activity ingestion, correction monitoring, action
      bundles, and weekly responsibility review.
- [ ] Implement weather/maps/local-activity sources and seasonal/household
      item workflows.
- [ ] Implement food, inventory, cart, order, refund, and delivery-recovery
      workflows.
- [ ] Implement deterministic childcare/work scenarios and source-grounded
      parenting guidance boundaries.
- [ ] Author and live-verify G1-G48 plus all ten Jordan co-parent scenarios.
- [ ] Reconcile every overlapping open LifeOps issue and PR; reuse valid work
      and close no item until the production path and evidence are complete.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every row in the design doc delivery ledger is complete.
- [ ] The busy world-traveling co-parent journey works from source ingestion
      through conflict discovery, privacy-preserving coordination, approval,
      materialization, change recovery, and closure.
- [ ] Loading, designed-empty, unavailable, stale, partial, and error states are
      distinguishable at every source boundary.
- [ ] No private event title, child-private fact, or unrelated adult data leaks
      across household scopes or exports.
- [ ] Duplicate/out-of-order provider events, retries, concurrent approvals,
      recurrence edits, DST/date-line crossings, and transaction retries are
      deterministic and idempotent.
- [ ] Real-provider or sandbox-provider contracts cover every connector; mocks
      and deterministic LLM fixtures are supplemental only.
- [ ] Live-model scenarios record inputs, provider context, actions, outputs,
      and domain artifacts, and every artifact is manually reviewed.
- [ ] Full package tests, repository verification, and all applicable UI,
      security, and evidence gates pass after rebasing on `origin/develop`.

## Evidence Plan

- [ ] Screenshots or recording: full desktop/mobile flow where UI applies;
      otherwise an explicit N/A reason per backend-only work item.
- [ ] Logs: structured backend logs plus frontend console/network logs where UI
      applies, including success, partial-source, stale, permission, and recovery
      paths.
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectories: JSON report, run viewer, and native JSONL for the
      persona and adversarial corpus, opened and reviewed by hand.
- [ ] Domain artifacts: calendar events/provider IDs, approvals, proposals,
      access grants, audit events/exports, source versions, scheduled tasks,
      carts/orders/receipts/refunds, and completion records.
- [ ] CI runs: scoped package lanes, full `bun run verify`, relevant real E2E
      lanes, and all PR checks.

## Dependencies / Sequencing

- Project: <https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/projects/15>
- Coordination: <https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/discussions/14407>
- Persona and journey workstream: <https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/discussions/14392>
- Process and evidence workstream: <https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/discussions/14406>
- Existing co-parent E2E: #14789
- Relationship inference/capture: #14785 and #14786
- Scheduling output proof: #14874
- Multi-account source ingestion: #14758 and #14792
- Existing LifeOps live verification: #16938 and #16941
- Side-effect receipts and final send-boundary proof: #17027

Sequence the truth and authorization layers before new convenience domains:
calendar/source health → proposals/access/audit → school/household sources →
food/transactions → financial/guidance surfaces → complete live persona proof.

topIssues.title: P0: agent deletion is failing 100% in production (160/160 jobs, 37 agents stuck) + 78% overall job failure rate
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## Summary

A live production audit of the provisioning pipeline (2026-07-29) found **agent deletion is failing 100% of the time**, and has been for days. This is customer-visible and accelerating.

Over the last 7 days: **554 failed jobs vs 153 completed** (78% failure rate).

## 1. `agent_delete` is completely broken — 160/160 failures, one identical cause

Every failed `agent_delete` job in the window carries the same error:

```
value.toISOString is not a function
```

- 160 failures, all identical, most recent **2026-07-28 18:03 UTC** (still current).
- All of them exhausted `attempts >= max_attempts` — so each one also burned the full retry budget.
- Consequence: **37 agents are stuck in `deletion_failed`**, up from 5 five days ago, and accelerating: **17 of them in the last 24 hours alone**.
- Customers who ask to delete an agent get a failure, the agent stays, and it keeps occupying node capacity.

`value.toISOString is not a function` is Drizzle's timestamp serializer receiving a **string where a `Date` is expected** — the same class as the cache/JSON round-trip defect fixed in #16859/#16860 for `resolveSharedAgent`.

One concrete candidate worth checking first (not yet proven to be the site): `prepareAgentBackupInsertData` (`packages/cloud/shared/src/db/repositories/agent-sandboxes.ts`) does

```ts
const createdAt = data.created_at ?? new Date();
// ...
created_at: createdAt,
```

`??` only guards `null`/`undefined` — a value that already crossed a JSON boundary as an ISO **string** passes straight through into the timestamp column. The 4 non-restart `agent_snapshot` failures in the same window are literally `Failed query: insert into "agent_sandbox_backups" (...)`, which is that insert.

## 2. `agent_snapshot`: 386 failures, 381 of them not the job's fault

```
Job interrupted by worker restart 2 times - max attempts reached   (381)
Failed query: insert into "agent_sandbox_backups" ...              (4)
Job timed out 2 times - max attempts reached                       (1)
```

The worker keeps restarting mid-snapshot, and **each restart consumes an attempt**. Two restarts exhaust `max_attempts` and the job is marked permanently failed — even though nothing about the job itself failed. A restart is an infrastructure event, not a job defect, and should not spend the job's retry budget (the codebase already has the shape for this: `retryLaterWithoutIncrementingAttempts`).

Why the worker restarts so often is the second half of this: it is consistent with the heap abort in #17154 and with the unbounded source-side snapshot capture in #17172 §1 (a large agent's capture is materialized entirely in the worker's heap).

## 3. The fleet is at or over capacity

| node | capacity | running |
|---|---|---|
| eliza-core-prod-2 | 24 | 24 |
| eliza-core-prod-3 | 24 | **25** |
| eliza-core-prod-4 | 24 | 24 |
| eliza-core-prod-5 | 24 | 24 |
| eliza-core-prod-6 | 24 | 24 |

prod-3 is **over** its declared capacity, and every robot is full, so new work is spilling onto autoscaled cloud nodes (3 × 4 running). Note the interaction: the 37 undeletable agents and the 45 in `error` are holding slots that should have been reclaimed — the delete failure is directly feeding the capacity pressure.

Also present: a `knowledge_processing` job stuck `in_progress` since **2025-12-31** (~7 months), which no sweeper has reclaimed.

## Why these compound

The three interact rather than being independent:
1. Deletes fail → agents accumulate (`deletion_failed` 37, `error` 45) → capacity fills.
2. Snapshots fail on worker restart → upgrades/deletes that depend on a restore point are less safe.
3. Full capacity → more scheduling pressure → longer boots → more exposure to the sweeper/timeout classes (#17215).

## Asks

- [ ] Pin and fix the `toISOString` write in the delete path — deterministic, 100% reproducible, highest customer impact.
- [ ] A worker restart must not consume a job's retry budget (`retryLaterWithoutIncrementingAttempts` semantics for interruption).
- [ ] Recover the 37 `deletion_failed` + 45 `error` rows once the above land (see #17162 for the 44-agent precedent and its recovery constraints).
- [ ] Reconcile declared capacity vs actual (prod-3 at 25/24), and reclaim the 7-month-stuck `in_progress` job.

Evidence gathered live against production (counts, error strings, timings; no customer identifiers). Related: #17215 (sweeper vs in-flight cold boots), #17154 (worker heap abort), #17172 (snapshot budgets), #17162 (the 2026-07-13 stranding), #17185 (delete must release capacity exactly once). [stan-cloud]

topPRs.title: release: promote develop to main (shared-tier shell probes + 249 commits)
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Production release: promotes `develop` → `main`, which deploys the Worker to `api.elizacloud.ai` and the Pages projects to the apex + `app.elizacloud.ai`.

## Why now

Headline fix: **Tier-0 shared agents 404'd every app-shell startup probe** (#17292). On a live shared agent the hosted app degraded through error paths — slash menu empty via a rejected catalog load, custom actions dropped, stream avatar warn, and the LifeOps capture loop re-reporting an "unexpected" failure on every signal. Production is the environment where that was observed, so the fix only helps once it lands here.

## Scope

- **249 commits**, 239 changed files under `packages/cloud/api` + `packages/cloud/shared`.
- **2 new production migrations**, both additive and idempotent — no destructive ops, no data rewrites:
  - `0183_lifecycle_execution_fence.sql` — `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` on `jobs`/`agent_sandboxes`, two partial `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, one `DO $$`-guarded CHECK constraint.
  - `0184_job_execution_leases.sql` — `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS job_execution_leases` + FK + index.

## Verification of the headline fix on staging

Already deployed to staging (`api-staging.elizacloud.ai`, commit `2c3d63d3849`) and verified over **real HTTP against a real Tier-0 shared agent** created on staging (`6a2dc51c-767f-43a8-9684-d5ad2b19f3c4`, `execution_tier: shared`):

| Probe | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `GET runtime/mode` | 404 | 200 `{"mode":"cloud","deploymentRuntime":"cloud",…}` |
| `GET commands?surface=gui` | 404 | 200 `{"commands":[]}` |
| `GET custom-actions` | 404 | 200 `{"actions":[]}` |
| `GET agent/events?limit=300` | 404 | 200 `{"events":[]}` |
| `GET stream/settings` | 404 | 200 `{"ok":true,"settings":{}}` |
| `POST apps/overlay-presence` | 404 | 200 `{"ok":true,"appName":null}` |
| `POST views/chat/navigate` | 404 | 200 `{"ok":true,"viewId":"chat",…}` |
| `POST lifeops/activity-signals` | 404 | 503 typed capability gate (the status the client's stop-latch recognizes) |
| `POST conversations/:id/greeting` | 404 | 200 `{"text":"","agentName":"ProbeVerify","generated":false,…}` |

Negative controls on the same live deployment — nothing is masked by a catch-all:

```
GET  totally-unknown                    -> 404
POST totally-unknown                    -> 404
POST views/workbench/navigate           -> 404   (view this tier does not serve)
POST conversations/<other-id>/greeting  -> 404   (non-canonical conversation)
GET  runtime/mode  (no API key)         -> 401   (no synthesized 200 without auth)
```

Environment isolation also confirmed live: a staging-minted key returns 200 on `api-staging` and **401** on `api.elizacloud.ai`.

## Evidence

<!-- evidence-row:after-screenshots -->

<!-- evidence-row:walkthrough-video -->
- [ ] N/A - release promote of already-reviewed commits; no new flow is introduced by this PR.
<!-- evidence-row:backend-logs -->

<!-- evidence-row:frontend-logs -->
- [x] [17300-frontend-console-before.log](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17300-frontend-console-before.log)
<!-- evidence-row:llm-trajectory -->
- [ ] N/A - no agent, action, provider, prompt, or model behavior is introduced by this promote; the shared-tier fix is REST synthesis with no model call.

topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Relates to #17175, #17176, #17177, #17178, #17179, and #17181.

The research, architecture, capability ledger, connector plan, persona,
48-scenario corpus, implementation phases, and evidence status are documented
in
[`packages/docs/ongoing-development/research/11-agentic-parent-suite.md`](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/feat/agentic-parent-suite/packages/docs/ongoing-development/research/11-agentic-parent-suite.md).

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is rebased onto the latest
      `origin/develop` with zero conflicts (`8132bc67366`).
- [x] `bun install` and `bun run verify` were run after sync.
- [ ] A reviewer can confirm the complete live-provider product journey without
      reading the code. This remains a draft because live OAuth/webhook/provider
      proof is incomplete and G1 correctly failed.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Rebased onto the latest `origin/develop`; zero conflicts.
- [x] `bun run verify` passes post-sync.

# Risks

**Large.** This is a broad foundation PR (297 files) spanning calendar source
identity, availability, recurrence/timezone behavior, native Apple permission
semantics, Google watch lifecycle, immutable approval and mutation receipts,
household resource capacity, personal-assistant domains, one shared scheduler,
connector contracts, UI, benchmark provenance, and a SQL migration.

Primary risks are incorrect authority or tenant binding, duplicated external
effects during retry, recurrence/DST mistakes, stale source truth, webhook
abuse, accidental data disclosure across households/calendars, native
permission-mode drift, and UI states that hide a partial provider failure. The
new paths fail closed, use source/tenant/version/idempotency bindings, and have
focused real-PGlite and contract coverage; live providers remain a draft gate.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Adds the full world-traveling co-parent persona and G1-G48 test catalog, plus
  a 12,792-word implementation report grounded in 31 official, research,
  safety, and first-person sources.
- Adds source-aware calendar availability across selected Google, Apple,
  Microsoft, and ICS feeds, including health/freshness/provenance and explicit
  partial/error states.
- Adds durable Google push-channel bindings, strict notification validation,
  dedupe/order checks, scheduled retries and renewals, restart reconstruction,
  quota classification, and controlled 410 resync.
- Adds immutable calendar mutation proposals, exact owner/editor routing,
  approval CAS, replay receipts, series/version/tenant/source binding, Apple
  add-only semantics, and truthful invitation decline behavior.
- Adds deterministic caregiver/vehicle/restraint capacity solving with
  authorization, accessibility, freshness, handoff, transition,
  distinct-resource, invalidation, and shared-review constraints.
- Extends one shared `ScheduledTask` architecture and typed dispatch results; it
  does not add a second scheduler.
- Adds school-source reconciliation, household operations, family
  communications, food/inventory, parenting guidance,
  weather/routes/activity oracle, and childcare/work-scenario foundations with
  explicit source and safety contracts.
- Adds a calendar source manager UI and native permission presentation, plus
  desktop/mobile screenshots and a walkthrough harness.
- Fixes LifeOpsBench acting-agent provenance so adapter/provider/model are
  distinct from evaluator/judge identity and incomplete artifacts are rejected.

## What kind of change is this?

Features, improvements, tests, documentation, and one additive database
migration.

# Documentation changes needed?

- [x] Documentation is required and included.
- [x] The MVP persona documentation and ongoing-development index are updated.
- [x] The detailed report records what exists, what is missing, which work
      belongs to the LLM, which pieces require deterministic
      primitives/connectors, human failure modes, implementation phases,
      G1-G48 scenarios, and the exact evidence contract.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

1. Read the executive status and capability ledger in the report linked above.
2. Inspect the calendar source manager screenshots/video and the real G1
   failure trajectory in the evidence rows.
3. Review the durable Google watch test, owner calendar mutation gateway
   integration test, and resource-capacity PGlite integration test.
4. Confirm the report's explicit `0/48 complete` statement before interpreting
   the implementation status.

## Detailed testing completed

- `bun install` completed in the clean rebased worktree, including the required
  971 MiB artifact sync.
- `bun run verify`: **578/578 successful Turbo tasks** across 254 packages;
  lint, build, typecheck, dependency/script audits, 8,661-test-file anti-focus
  scan, and 28 dist-path consumer checks passed.
- Complete personal-assistant suite: **1,629 passed in 204 files, 8 intentional
  skips**, followed by a clean package TypeScript check.
- Calendar connector/service suite: **348 passed, 2 intentional live-provider
  skips**; Google connector suite 38 passed; connector shim 30 passed;
  public-route audit 5 passed.
- Source manager: 60 component/hook assertions and 63 focused
  accessibility/visual checks passed; five rendered iterations were reviewed.
- Immutable calendar mutation and owner-editor paths: 31 real-PGlite
  integration cases; EventEditor/routes/client contracts: 35 cases.
- Native Apple seam: 7 cases; Swift bridge contract: 15 cases.
- Household resource capacity: 15 real-PGlite cases; owner/affected-party
  resolution: 20 cases.
- LifeOpsBench changed-area regressions: 62 passed under Python 3.12.
- Focused evidence rerun: Google watch 8 passed; owner mutation gateway 13
  passed; resource capacity 15 passed.
- App audit: 252 views, 218 good, 25 manual-review, 9 pre-existing unrelated
  `needs-work`, 0 broken. Calendar desktop was good; three smaller calendar
  viewports were manually reviewed with no reported
  quality/console/overflow/color/hover defect.
- iOS cloud simulator build/install/launch succeeded. A real EventKit
  transaction was not possible without a reachable authenticated cloud
  backend.
- Real G1 model run: 12 turns with an acting-agent/evaluator/judge provenance
  chain and workload hash. It scored 0.0 and was manually reviewed. It repeated
  generic calendar searches, lacked a source-connect action, invented contact
  details, attempted an unapproved write, and then duplicated it. This is useful
  failure evidence, not a passing journey.

# Evidence Gate

<!-- evidence-row:before-screenshots -->
- [x] ![before-screenshots](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-calendar-source-before.jpg)
<!-- evidence-row:after-screenshots -->
- [x] ![after-screenshots](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-calendar-source-after.jpg)
<!-- evidence-row:walkthrough-video -->
- [x] https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-calendar-source-walkthrough.mp4
<!-- evidence-row:backend-logs -->
- [x] [17206-backend-domain-tests.log](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-backend-domain-tests.log)
<!-- evidence-row:frontend-logs -->
- [x] [17206-app-audit-report.json](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-app-audit-report.json)
<!-- evidence-row:llm-trajectory -->
- [x] [17206-g1-live-failure-trajectory.json](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-g1-live-failure-trajectory.json)
<!-- evidence-row:domain-artifacts -->
- [x] [17206-verify.log](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-verify.log)
<!-- evidence-row:ocr-review -->
- [x] [17206-calendar-source-ocr-review.json](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/releases/download/pr-evidence-2/17206-calendar-source-ocr-review.json)

# Evidence Details

The evidence rows will contain JPG desktop/mobile before and after comparisons,
MP4 source-manager walkthrough, real-PGlite backend logs, the full app audit
report, OCR review, the provenance-valid G1 live trajectory, the clean
repository verification log, and iOS build/install/launch proof. Every artifact
was manually inspected and secret-scanned before upload.

## Known gaps / failures

- **0 of G1-G48 currently satisfies the complete live evidence contract.** The
  report says this explicitly and lists the missing proof per scenario family.
- The most important newly observed product gap is an agent-facing typed source
  list/select/connect/reconnect action. Owner UI/routes exist, but the acting
  agent could not invoke them in G1.
- Live multi-account Google/Microsoft OAuth, shared/guest grant acquisition,
  Apple EventKit mutation, uniquely routed public Google webhook delivery,
  provider WAF/rate-limit proof, and real-provider receipt review remain
  pending.
- Raw school inbox/document/photo/portal ingestion, real maps/travel-time
  composition, production grocery inventory/purchase, authenticated family
  messaging/reply, and acoustic speaker identity remain incomplete.
- The global app audit is not represented as clean: it passed 253 Playwright
  checks but its ratchet remains red because of nine unrelated pre-existing
  views.
- The iOS evidence proves the exact branch built, installed, and launched; it
  does not prove EventKit execution because no authenticated cloud backend was
  reachable.
- The real G1 trajectory is a failed run and must not be treated as qualifying
  success evidence.
- The exhaustive Python benchmark suite was not completed; the 62 directly
  affected Python 3.12 regressions passed. The full TypeScript
  personal-assistant suite and repository-wide verify both completed.

This PR stays draft until reviewers decide whether to split the broad foundation
or continue adding live-provider evidence on this branch.

topPRs.title: fix: repair reviewed runtime and develop CI regressions
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Relates to #13406 and the reviewed open-PR queue.

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is based on the latest `origin/develop`
      (`769b017123c8e01b46cc9a5785e4c47382dbd3f9`) with zero conflicts.
- [x] Dependencies were installed and the requested lint, build, and typecheck
      gates were run after the final repair.
- [x] A reviewer can confirm the UI portion from the attached screenshots,
      walkthrough, OCR report, and exact automated test results.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Fetched the latest `origin/develop`; the branch base is its current head.
- [x] `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, and `bun run typecheck` pass post-sync.

# Risks

Large. This consolidates independently reviewed repairs across cloud lifecycle
fencing, document queries, approval execution, Android startup/deep links,
Linux ISO proof, browser contracts, and shared UI shell behavior. The main
risks are cross-package contract drift and platform-specific CI behavior.
Those are covered by focused integration suites, full monorepo gates, the app
visual audit, and the exact-head PR workflow matrix.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

This is the integration branch produced by the open-PR review queue. It keeps
only reviewed, production-oriented repairs and addresses the real failures
observed on the current `develop` head:

- fences cloud provisioning job ownership, generations, recovery, and cleanup;
- unifies bounded document-list semantics across core, SQL, and in-memory stores;
- makes approvals subject-scoped, replay-safe, and delivery-observable;
- repairs Android first-run, deep-link replay, and device harness contracts;
- makes Linux ISO dependency resolution and boot proof deterministic;
- repairs Home/Launcher navigation, route ownership, auth startup, view lifecycle,
  streaming cadence, and cross-platform browser fixtures;
- keeps real network tests out of ordinary unit lanes while preserving explicit
  post-merge execution;
- hardens Windows path handling and script/JUnit result validation;
- installs lockfile-matched Playwright Chromium before Nightly runs the real browser-extension smoke.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fixes and test/CI reliability improvements. No intentional breaking API
change.

# Documentation changes needed?

Documentation was updated where the Linux OS build and verification contracts
changed. Other repairs preserve existing public contracts.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

Start with the commits grouped by subsystem, then the exact failure repairs:

- `c24199d915a` Windows/script/JUnit failure visibility
- `f1e3fdcaebc` and `b0f9769953d` Home/Launcher real-input navigation
- `96f589cfa58` cloud provisioning execution fencing
- `02beecd1bbe` document authorization and mutation contracts
- `9e40e253f06` approval subject access and provider delivery
- `9c48d3947b7` shared real-test lane isolation
- `9f43ff09416` Nightly Playwright provisioning and canonical browser-smoke resolution

## Detailed testing steps

- `bun run lint` - 235/235 tasks passed.
- `bun run build` - 176/176 tasks passed; view bundle guard 27/27.
- `bun run typecheck` - 343/343 tasks passed.
- `bun run --cwd packages/app audit:app` - 254 Playwright captures passed;
  computed verdicts: 0 broken, 0 needs-work.
- `bun run --cwd packages/shared test` - 114 files, 1,296 tests passed.
- Shared test inventory: real wake-word packaging absent by default, present

topPRs.title: fix: own latency and streaming lifecycles end to end
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Closes #17308.

## What changed

This integrates the reviewed latency/streaming work as one rebased branch on current `develop`:

- removes guessed chat, message-service, Discord, desktop proxy, and orchestrator generation deadlines;
- propagates caller/lifecycle cancellation through chat routes, message dispatch, model streaming, native bridges, local inference, Discord delivery, desktop IPC, Android and iOS;
- replaces orchestrator polling with ready/reconnected events and awaited shutdown drains;
- preserves upstream Discord exact-delivery receipts and audience attestation;
- parallelizes dependency-safe plugin/provider/database work, batches relationship entity reads, removes duplicate relationship ownership, and coalesces document authorization within the turn-owned memo;
- makes embedding metadata declarative rather than fabricating probe vectors;
- accelerates and owns Android Kokoro PCM/TTS streaming;
- keeps performance CI informational and removes threshold/ratchet/changed-source-test gating;
- adds real provider, chat-path, browser/PGLite, native, cancellation, and lifecycle telemetry/tests.

## Current exact telemetry

Latest 50-sample PGLite provider sweep on this branch (24/24 providers):

- fresh compose: p50 6.231 ms, p95 7.383 ms, max 8.017 ms
- maximum same-turn reuse: p50 0.058 ms, p95 0.096 ms, max 0.153 ms
- effective parallelism: approximately 5x
- slowest provider: DOCUMENTS p50 6.130 ms, p95 7.242 ms, max 7.841 ms
- next: RELATIONSHIPS p95 3.962 ms; FACTS p95 3.904 ms

Real production-route browser/PGLite delivery trace:

- total 168 ms with a deliberately delayed 103 ms model stream
- time to first model token 40 ms; validated visible reply 161 ms
- message-service exclusive overhead 6.608 ms
- providers 10.392 ms; ingress 6.659 ms; delivery persistence 5 ms
- provider -> validated SSE -> React -> PGLite -> pixels were byte-identical

Independent framework-only benchmark, 50 turns:

- median 2.15 ms; p95 3.63 ms; p99 5.57 ms
- 425.4 messages/sec

## Verification

- Discord: 61 files, 461 tests passed; typecheck and lint passed.
- Agent orchestrator: 2,603 passed, 13 skipped; one live Gemma test failed only on Cerebras HTTP 402 quota.
- Core focused latency/cancellation/provider/document suites passed; core typecheck passed.
- Agent chat/usage focused suites passed; full package suite reached live Cerebras and failed only on HTTP 402 quota.
- Real browser + production conversation route + PGLite + React test passed.
- Native llama/Kokoro branch built and tested with NDK/Gradle and is pushed separately at elizaOS/llama.cpp `eliza/kokoro-owned-pcm-v15`.

## Live-model evidence blocker

Cerebras `gemma-4-31b` currently returns:

```json
{"message":"Payment required to access this resource. Visit your billing tab.","type":"payment_required_error","param":"quota","code":"payment_required"}
```

The live tests deliberately fail and report that provider response. Nothing is mocked, skipped, retried behind a deadline, or reported as a pass. Re-run the existing live workflow after quota is restored.

## Evidence applicability

- Screenshots/video: N/A — no visual product design change; browser pixels are exercised by the real delivery E2E.
- Live trajectory: blocked by the exact Cerebras 402 above.
- Backend/client/network/domain evidence: generated locally and summarized above; full provider and inference JSON reports are available from the repository scripts/workflow artifacts.
